messages.content:
You are given one person (a thinker), the lead section of their encyclopedia article (EXTRACT), and a list of historical events and periods whose dates overlap the person's life (EVENTS, each with an id).

Say which of the listed events bear on this person, and how. Use only the EXTRACT: if the extract does not mention or clearly imply an event, do not connect it, even if you know the connection from elsewhere. An event that merely happened during the person's life is not a connection unless the extract brings it up.

For each connection give:
- "event": the id from the EVENTS list, exactly as written (Q followed by digits). Never an event that is not in the list.
- "type", one of:
  - "lived_through": the extract mentions the event as part of the person's circumstances, without saying they acted in it or wrote against it;
  - "took_part_in": the person acted in the event (fought, sat in the assembly, negotiated, signed, governed, led);
  - "wrote_in_response_to": a named work, or the person's writing generally, answers or treats the event; put the work's title in "work" if the extract names one;
  - "suffered_under": the person was exiled, imprisoned, censored, dismissed, persecuted or killed because of the event;
  - "shaped_by": the extract says the event formed the person's thinking, without naming a work.
- "reason": one sentence in your own words.
- "evidence": one sentence copied exactly from the EXTRACT, character for character, that supports the connection. Do not paraphrase, shorten or join sentences.
- "work": the title of the work, if the type is wrote_in_response_to and the extract names it; otherwise an empty string.

If an event in the list is the same thing under a broader or narrower name as one the extract mentions (the extract says "the civil war" and the list has "English Civil War"), connect it. If nothing in the extract bears on any listed event, return an empty list. Return JSON only, matching the schema you are given.

PERSON: Antiochus of Ascalon (129 BCE–67 BCE). ancient Greek philosopher

EXTRACT:
Antiochus of Ascalon (; Ancient Greek: Άντίοχος ὁ Ἀσκαλώνιος; c. 135/130 – c. 68 BC) was a 1st-century BC Platonist philosopher. He rejected skepticism, blended Stoic doctrines with Platonism, and was
the first philosopher in the tradition of Middle Platonism.
Antiochus moved to Athens early in his life and became a pupil of Philo of Larissa at the Platonic Academy, but he went on to reject the prevailing Academic skepticism of Philo and his predecessors. This led to his resignation from the academy and the establishment of his own school, which he named the "Old Academy" as he claimed it was closer to original doctrines of Platonism that he believed had been betrayed by the skeptics of the New Academy under Philo. His students at this new institution included the Roman politicians Varro and Cicero. Antiochus was also the friend of the Roman politician and general Lucullus, whom he accompanied on a trip to North Africa and on a campaign to Armenia.
After the decline of the New Academy in the late 1st century BC, his school was the sole inheritor of the Platonic tradition in Athens, which began the period of philosophy known as Middle Platonism. Antiochus endeavoured to bring some doctrines of the Stoics and the Peripatetics into Platonism, and stated, in opposition to Philo, that the mind could distinguish true from false, following the Stoic doctrine of katalepsis. In doing so, he claimed to be reviving the doctrines of the Old Academy. Despite his emphasis on the Platonic tradition, his ideas were often more Stoic than Platonist; in particular, he gave up the Platonic philosophy of transcendence in favor of a materialistic doctrine of nature.

Q903199  Cimbrian War (-112–-100) — war bewteen Rome and a union of Germanic and Celtic tribes, 113-101 BCE
Q1616064  Mithridatic Wars (-87–-62) — 1st-century BCE wars between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Pontus
Q1647768  First Mithridatic War (-88–-84) — war between the Roman Republic and king Mithridates VI of Pontus, 89-84 BCE
Q1764124  Third Mithridatic War (-72–-62) — war between Pontus and its allies and the Roman Republic
